question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

Harry stepped in, his head almost ______ the sloping ceiling, and blinked.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. touching.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Touching means coming into contact with something, usually lightly. (छूना / स्पर्श करना)

◦ The sentence describes a tall person entering a room with a low sloping ceiling — his head very nearly comes into contact with it, so "almost touching" is the natural collocation.

◦ Correct: Harry stepped in, his head almost touching the sloping ceiling, and blinked.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Embracing" means hugging someone warmly or accepting an idea — a ceiling cannot be embraced by a head.

• "Grasping" means seizing something firmly with the hand, which a head cannot do.

• "Cuddling" means holding someone close affectionately, which is unsuitable for an inanimate ceiling.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: touch the sky, touch a nerve, keep in touch, a touching story (moving).

• "Embrace" also has a figurative sense: *She embraced the new technology* (accepted it willingly).

question: Four sentences are given, out of which three have spelling errors. Choose the sentence with all correctly spelt words.
option_1: I was a bit depressed by our apparant lack of progress.
option_2: Urban dwellers often accept noise as part of city life.
option_3: She is going to divorce him on the grounds of adultary.
option_4: Its sanctions are based on compairisons between the two companies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Urban dwellers often accept noise as part of city life.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 2 — *urban, dwellers, accept, noise* — is correctly spelt, so it is the only error-free sentence. (नगरवासी)

◦ Note the pair accept (to receive/agree) vs except (other than); the sentence uses "accept" correctly.

◦ Correct: Urban dwellers often accept noise as part of city life.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "apparant" is wrong; the correct spelling is apparent (spelt with -ent).

• Option 3: "adultary" is wrong; the correct spelling is adultery (extramarital relations).

• Option 4: "compairisons" is wrong; the correct spelling is comparisons (no 'i' after 'a').

NOTE

• Frequently misspelt SSC words: occurrence, embarrass, maintenance, privilege, separate, definitely, harass.

• Do not confuse adultery (infidelity) with adulteration (mixing impurities in food).

question: Four words are given, out of which three words are spelt correctly. Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. VISCIOUS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is VICIOUS (V-I-C-I-O-U-S), meaning cruel, violent or savage. (क्रूर / हिंसक)

◦ The printed form "VISCIOUS" wrongly inserts an 's' — it appears to blend *vicious* with *viscous* (thick and sticky).

◦ Correct: The dog gave him a vicious bite.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "STILETTOS" is correct — women's shoes with very high thin heels (also a slender dagger).

• "BEWILDERS" is correct — puzzles or confuses someone completely.

• "UNFORESEEN" is correct — not anticipated or predicted in advance.

NOTE

• Distinguish vicious (cruel) from viscous (thick liquid, like honey) — both are asked in SSC spelling sets.

• Common idiom: a vicious circle — a situation in which one problem causes another, which worsens the first.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

A historical account or biography written from personal knowledge
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Memoir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A memoir is a historical account or biography written from personal knowledge or special sources — a record of one's own experiences. (संस्मरण)

◦ The key element in the definition is *personal knowledge*, which points precisely to "memoir".

◦ Correct: Her memoir of the war years became a bestseller.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Chronicle" — a factual record of events arranged in order of time, not necessarily personal.

• "Thesis" — a long research dissertation submitted for an academic degree.

• "Blog" — a regularly updated website or web page written in an informal, conversational style.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: Autobiography (life story written by oneself), Biography (life story written by another), Diary (daily personal record), Anthology (collection of poems/stories).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

Though they allow celebrities and famous people to take pictures (inside the museum, but they does not allow the general public) to do the same.
option_1: inside the museum, they do not allow the general public
option_3: inside the museum, but do not allowing the general public
option_4: inside the museum, they does not allow general public
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. inside the museum, they do not allow the general public.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence already begins with the subordinating conjunction "Though", so adding "but" in the main clause is a double conjunction error. Use one connector, not two. (दोहरा संयोजक अशुद्धि)

◦ The plural pronoun "they" takes the plural verb "do", never "does"; also "the general public" needs the definite article the.

◦ Correct: Though they allow celebrities and famous people to take pictures inside the museum, they do not allow the general public to do the same.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is wrong because the bracketed part has both a "though…but" error and a subject-verb agreement error.

• Option 3 "but do not allowing" is wrong — "do not" must be followed by the bare infinitive "allow", not "allowing".

• Option 4 keeps the wrong verb "does" with "they" and drops the article before "general public".

NOTE

• Never pair these: Though/Although…but, Because…so, As…therefore, Unless…not.

• Correct: *Although he was tired, he finished the work* (no "but").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

I assisted him to undo the (task after I finished my work).
option_1: task after I will finish my work
option_3: task after I will have finished my work
option_4: task after I had finished my work
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. task after I had finished my work.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When two past actions are described, the earlier action takes the past perfect (had + V3) and the later action takes the simple past. (पूर्ण भूतकाल)

◦ Here "finishing my work" happened before "assisting him", so it must be had finished, while the main verb "assisted" stays in the simple past.

◦ Correct: I assisted him to undo the task after I had finished my work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "will finish" mixes a future tense with the past verb "assisted" — a tense-sequence error.

• Option 2 is wrong because the simple past "finished" fails to show that the action was completed earlier.

• Option 3 "will have finished" is future perfect and again clashes with the past main clause.

NOTE

• Rule of past perfect: had + V3 for the first of two past actions; often with *after, before, when, by the time*.

• Example: *The train had left before we reached the station.*

question:
Select the word from the options which is exactly opposite in meaning to the bracketed word given in the sentence below.

The pandemic has seen soaring home prices and record housing (insecurity).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Firmness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Insecurity means a lack of stability, safety or confidence — a state of uncertainty. (असुरक्षा / अस्थिरता)

• Firmness means steadiness, stability and resolute confidence, which is exactly the opposite of insecurity. (दृढ़ता / स्थिरता)

◦ Correct: The pandemic has seen soaring home prices and record housing insecurity; the antonym of the bracketed word is firmness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Hesitancy" means reluctance or wavering — a synonym, not an antonym, of insecurity.

• "Pretence" means a false show or make-believe; it is unrelated to the idea of stability.

• "Self-doubt" means lack of confidence in oneself — again close in meaning to insecurity.

NOTE

• Synonyms of insecurity: instability, vulnerability, anxiety, uncertainty, precariousness.

• Synonyms of firmness: steadfastness, resolve, solidity, determination, stability.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Eight years ago, she founded / Humans of Bombay, inspired of / the single idea – we all want to be heard.
option_1: the single idea – we all want to be heard.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Humans of Bombay, inspired of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "inspire" takes the preposition by when it names the source of the inspiration — *inspired by something/someone*, never "inspired of". (प्रेरित होना)

◦ "Inspired" here is a past participle used as a reduced passive; the agent after a passive participle is introduced by by.

◦ Correct: Eight years ago, she founded Humans of Bombay, inspired by the single idea – we all want to be heard.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Eight years ago, she founded" is correct — "ago" is properly used with the simple past.

• Option 1 "the single idea – we all want to be heard." is correct — the dash introduces an explanatory clause.

• Option 3 is wrong because the sentence does contain a preposition error.

NOTE

• Fixed prepositions: inspired by, influenced by, accompanied by, surrounded by, impressed by/with.

• But note: inspiration for something, and inspired to + verb (*She was inspired to write*).

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

The branch of physics concerned with the properties of sound
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Acoustics.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Acoustics is the branch of physics that deals with sound — its production, transmission and effects. (ध्वनि विज्ञान)

◦ It also refers to the sound quality of a hall: *The acoustics of the auditorium are excellent.*

◦ Correct: Acoustics is the branch of physics concerned with the properties of sound.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Anchor" — a heavy device that keeps a ship in place, or a person who presents a TV programme.

• "Anarchist" — a person who believes government and law should be abolished.

• "Apiary" — a place where bees are kept for their honey.

NOTE

• Related branches: Optics (light), Entomology (insects), Ornithology (birds), Seismology (earthquakes), Numismatics (coins).

• Related places: Aviary (birds), Apiary (bees), Aquarium (fish), Hive (bee colony).

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Satisfactory
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Inadequate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Satisfactory means good enough, acceptable or fulfilling the required standard. (संतोषजनक)

• Inadequate means insufficient or not good enough for the purpose — the exact opposite. (अपर्याप्त)

◦ Correct: His performance was far from satisfactory; in fact it was inadequate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Revive" is a verb meaning to bring back to life or restore; it is not an adjective and cannot be an antonym here.

• "Morose" means gloomy and bad-tempered — the opposite of cheerful, not of satisfactory.

• "Diminish" is a verb meaning to make or become less.

NOTE

• Synonyms of satisfactory: adequate, acceptable, sufficient, passable, up to the mark.

• Other antonyms: unsatisfactory, deficient, substandard, poor, wanting.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Enthuse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fondle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Enthuse means to show or express great excitement and eagerness about something, or to make someone enthusiastic. (उत्साहित करना)

• Of the four choices, only Fondle carries a positive, affectionate feeling; the other three — *unbothered, carefree, lazy* — all suggest indifference or lack of interest, i.e. the opposite of enthusiasm.

◦ Correct (as per the official key): The synonym of "Enthuse" is Fondle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Unbothered" means not worried or not concerned — the antonym of an enthusiastic attitude.

• "Carefree" means free from anxiety or responsibility, which is not the same as being eager.

• "Lazy" means unwilling to work or use energy — clearly opposite to enthusiasm.

NOTE

• True synonyms of enthuse: *rave, gush, be excited about, rhapsodise, motivate, inspire*. Antonyms: *bore, dampen, discourage*.

• The tick in the official answer key is on Option 3 ("Fondle"), so it has been recorded as the answer, although "fondle" (to caress/stroke lovingly) is not a true dictionary synonym of "enthuse" — treat this as a defective SSC item and go with the key.

question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text. Select the option with correct idiom for the bracketed text.

You all look great in your costumes! (Good luck!)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Break a leg.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Break a leg is a theatrical idiom used to wish a performer good luck before going on stage. (शुभकामनाएँ देना)

◦ The context — people in costumes about to perform — makes this the perfect substitution for "Good luck!".

◦ Correct: You all look great in your costumes! Break a leg!

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Come again" means "please repeat what you said" — a request for repetition.

• "Don't swear it" is not a standard English idiom.

• "Spit it out" means to say what you are hesitating to say, quickly and directly.

NOTE

• Other good-luck expressions: fingers crossed, knock 'em dead, best of luck.

• More stage idioms: steal the show (win all the praise), in the limelight (at the centre of attention), wait in the wings (be ready for one's chance).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A bad egg
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A bad person.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a bad egg" refers to a dishonest, worthless or troublesome person — someone of bad character. (बुरा व्यक्ति)

◦ The opposite idiom is "a good egg", meaning a thoroughly likeable, decent person.

◦ Correct: Don't trust him with the money; he has always been a bad egg.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "A very small insignificant amount" is the meaning of a drop in the ocean, not of "a bad egg".

• "To be frustrated" is expressed by idioms like at one's wits' end or fed up.

• "To calm down" corresponds to cool off or simmer down.

NOTE

• More 'person' idioms: a black sheep (disgrace to the family), a wolf in sheep's clothing (a hidden enemy), a fair-weather friend (a friend only in good times), a big fish (an important person).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Bushfire in Australia has ______ the conditions of many animals in the forest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. worsened.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Worsened means made or become worse — a decline in condition. (बदतर करना / बिगाड़ना)

◦ A bushfire is a destructive event, so it can only make the condition of forest animals worse; the sentence needs a negative-impact verb.

◦ Correct: Bushfire in Australia has worsened the conditions of many animals in the forest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Fortified" means strengthened or reinforced — a positive sense, unsuitable after a disaster.

• "Maintained" means kept in the same state, which contradicts the destructive effect of a fire.

• "Surpassed" means exceeded or went beyond; it does not collocate with "conditions".

NOTE

• Synonyms of worsen: deteriorate, aggravate, exacerbate, decline. Antonyms: improve, ameliorate, better.

• Note the spelling pair: aggravate (make worse) vs irritate (annoy).

question:
Select the word from the options which is similar in meaning to the bracketed part given in the sentence below.

I was (feeling afraid) that something bad would happen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Scared.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Scared means frightened or afraid — exactly the sense of the bracketed phrase "feeling afraid". (डरा हुआ)

◦ After the verb "was", an adjective is required, and "scared" fits both the meaning and the grammar.

◦ Correct: I was scared that something bad would happen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Sacred" means holy or connected with religion — a common spelling trap with "scared".

• "Divine" means godlike or heavenly, again unrelated to fear.

• "Bold" means brave and confident, which is the very opposite of feeling afraid.

NOTE

• Synonyms of scared: terrified, frightened, petrified, apprehensive, panic-stricken.

• Watch these look-alike pairs: scared/sacred, desert/dessert, quite/quiet, angle/angel.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Raising temperatures in the springtime signal plants and animals to come alive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Raising temperatures in the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rise" is an intransitive verb (rise – rose – risen) meaning to go up by itself, while "raise" is transitive (raise – raised – raised) and needs an object. (स्वयं बढ़ना बनाम बढ़ाना)

◦ Temperatures go up on their own, so the participial adjective must be rising, not "raising".

◦ Correct: Rising temperatures in the springtime signal plants and animals to come alive.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "springtime signal plants and" is correct — the plural verb "signal" agrees with the plural subject "temperatures".

• Option 3 "animals to come alive." is correct — "signal + object + to-infinitive" is a standard structure.

• Option 4 is wrong because the sentence does contain an error in the first part.

NOTE

• Similar transitive/intransitive pairs: lie (lay, lain) vs lay (laid, laid); sit vs set; fall vs fell.

• Correct usage: *The sun rises in the east*; *He raised his hand*.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There was a general hesitation and ______ to ignore the problem.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Demur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Demur as a noun means hesitation, objection or reluctance; as a verb it means to raise doubts or object. (आपत्ति / हिचकिचाहट)

◦ The blank is joined by "and" to the noun "hesitation", so it needs a noun of similar meaning — "demur" fits both grammatically and in sense.

◦ Correct: There was a general hesitation and demur to ignore the problem.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Disposition" means a person's natural temperament or an inclination — an inclination *to ignore* would contradict "hesitation".

• "Deride" is a verb meaning to mock or ridicule, so it cannot follow "hesitation and".

• "Denigrate" is also a verb, meaning to criticise unfairly or belittle someone.

NOTE

• Common phrase: without demur — without objecting or hesitating (*He agreed without demur*).

• Synonyms of demur: objection, protest, reservation, qualm, misgiving.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Look in a mirror and take your ______ with each step.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Take your time is a fixed idiomatic phrase meaning to do something slowly and carefully, without hurrying. (जल्दबाज़ी न करना)

◦ The possessive "your" before the blank signals the idiom "take one's time"; the advice to watch each step in a mirror supports this sense.

◦ Correct: Look in a mirror and take your time with each step.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Plague" means a deadly epidemic disease or, as a verb, to trouble someone constantly — it does not fit "take your ___".

• "Ages" means a very long time, but "take your ages" is not idiomatic English ("it takes ages" is).

• "Hostage" means a captive; one takes *someone* hostage, not "your hostage" in this context.

NOTE

• Other "take" idioms: take after (resemble), take off (leave the ground / remove), take up (start a hobby), take to task (scold), take for granted (undervalue).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Have you ever gone into/ a high-street shop wearing/ a pair of cycling shorts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is grammatically sound throughout, so "No error" is the right choice. (कोई त्रुटि नहीं)

◦ Have you ever gone into — the present perfect with "ever" is standard for asking about experience, and "gone into" (entered) takes "into" correctly.

◦ a pair of cycling shorts — plural-only garments (shorts, trousers, jeans, scissors) are counted with "a pair of".

◦ Correct: Have you ever gone into a high-street shop wearing a pair of cycling shorts? — no change needed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "Have you ever gone into" is correct — "gone" is the past participle required after "have".

• Option 2 "a high-street shop wearing" is correct — "wearing" is a participial phrase modifying "you", and the compound adjective "high-street" is properly hyphenated before the noun.

• Option 1 "a pair of cycling shorts?" is correct in both article and number.

NOTE

• Have been to = visited and returned; have gone to = went and is still there — a favourite SSC distinction.

• Always "a pair of" with: spectacles, tongs, pyjamas, binoculars, pliers.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

She was born with full sight and hearing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In "full sight and hearing", the adjective full correctly modifies the two nouns sight and hearing after the preposition "with". (पूर्ण दृष्टि एवं श्रवण-शक्ति)

◦ A preposition must be followed by a noun or noun phrase, and "full sight" is a perfectly formed noun phrase; the parallel noun "hearing" confirms it.

◦ Correct: She was born with full sight and hearing. — no change is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "full sighting" is wrong — "sighting" means the act of spotting something (*a rare bird sighting*), not the sense of vision.

• Option 2 "fully sight" is wrong — the adverb "fully" cannot modify the noun "sight"; adverbs modify verbs/adjectives.

• Option 3 "full sighted" is wrong — "sighted" is an adjective and would not run parallel with the noun "hearing"; the standard adjective is "fully sighted" used before a noun.

NOTE

• Adjective + noun after a preposition: *with great care*, *in full swing*, *at short notice*.

• Related words: sight (vision), sightseeing (visiting places of interest), insight (deep understanding), oversight (an unintentional omission).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. within.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Within is the preposition used before a period of time to mean "before the end of that period" — *within minutes, within a week*. (के भीतर)

◦ The passage says allergies begin to act up very soon after the earrings go in, so "within minutes of putting earrings in your ears" is the natural expression.

◦ Correct: Metal allergies can begin to act up within minutes of putting earrings in your ears.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "of" cannot introduce a time span after "act up"; it would leave the sentence meaningless.

• "about" would mean "approximately", but it does not fit before "minutes of putting".

• "with" indicates accompaniment or means, not a period of time.

NOTE

• Time prepositions: in (a month/year), on (a day/date), at (a clock time), within (before the end of a period), by (not later than).

• Phrasal verb here: act up — to start causing trouble or behaving badly.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. take.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb take out means to remove something from a place — the standard verb used for removing earrings. (निकालना)

◦ The structure "having to ______ the earrings out" needs a bare infinitive after "to", and only "take" forms an idiomatic phrasal verb with the particle "out" here.

◦ Correct: Some people can go a few hours before having to take the earrings out.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Expel" means to force someone to leave a school or country, or to drive something out forcefully — too strong and wrong in register.

• "Make … out" means to manage to see or understand something, which does not suit removing jewellery.

• "Hand out" means to distribute something to a group of people.

NOTE

• Useful "take" phrasal verbs: take off (remove/leave the ground), take in (absorb/deceive), take over (assume control), take back (retract).

• Separable phrasal verbs allow both "take out the earrings" and "take the earrings out".

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. discomfort.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Discomfort means slight pain or physical uneasiness — precisely what a metal allergy causes. (असुविधा / तकलीफ़)

◦ The collocation "stand the discomfort" (= endure the irritation) fits the contrast introduced by "but some can barely…".

◦ Correct: … but some can barely stand the discomfort enough to bother putting earrings in at all.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "bomb" is an explosive device and has no connection with an allergic reaction.

• "knife" is a cutting tool; the passage describes irritation, not injury by a blade.

• "burn" refers to an injury from fire or heat — an allergy causes itching and soreness, not a burn.

NOTE

• Here stand = tolerate/endure, as in *I can't stand the noise*.

• Synonyms of discomfort: uneasiness, irritation, soreness, distress, inconvenience.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. who.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The relative pronoun who is used for people and functions as the subject of the relative clause. (कर्ता के लिए प्रयुक्त संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम)

◦ In "those of us ______ love to wear earrings", the blank is the subject of the verb "love", and the antecedent "us" refers to persons — so who is required.

◦ Correct: This can be discouraging for those of us who love to wear earrings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "whom" is the object form of "who"; here the pronoun is the subject, so "whom" is wrong.

• "which" is used only for things and animals, not for people.

• "that" cannot be used after the pattern "those of us", which idiomatically takes "who".

NOTE

• Quick test: replace with he/him — if he fits, use who; if him fits, use whom.

• Relative pronouns: who/whom (persons), which (things), whose (possession), that (persons or things, defining clauses only).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Metal allergies can begin to act up (1) ______ minutes of putting earrings in your ears. Some people can go a few hours before having to (2) ______ the earrings out, but some can barely stand the (3) ______ enough to bother putting earrings in at all. This can be discouraging for those of us (4) ______ love to wear earrings, but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for (5) ______ ears exists!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sensitive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sensitive means easily affected or irritated — the standard word used for skin or body parts that react to metals or chemicals. (संवेदनशील)

◦ Hypoallergenic jewellery is specifically designed for people with allergies, so it is made for sensitive ears.

◦ Correct: … but fortunately hypoallergenic jewellery for sensitive ears exists!

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "rustic" means rural or countryside-like in style; it cannot describe ears.

• "soft" describes texture and does not convey the idea of an allergic reaction.

• "modern" means belonging to the present time and has no link with allergies.

NOTE

• Hypoallergenic = designed to cause the fewest possible allergic reactions (*hypo-* = under/less).

• Do not confuse sensitive (easily affected emotionally/physically) with sensible (having good judgement) — a very common SSC confusable pair.

question: The terms = Dribbling, passing, shooting are associated with which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Basketball.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dribbling, passing and shooting are the three fundamental skills of Basketball. (बास्केटबॉल)

• Basketball was invented by Dr. James Naismith in 1891 at Springfield, Massachusetts, USA.

• A basketball team has 5 players on court; the governing body is FIBA (founded 1932, HQ — Mies, Switzerland).

• Other basketball terms: slam dunk, rebound, layup, travelling, blocking, pivot, free throw.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shooting — a target sport; terms: bull's eye, trigger, range, air rifle, pistol.

• Badminton — terms: smash, drop shot, deuce, shuttle, love, let, drive.

• Cricket — terms: googly, LBW, maiden over, stumped, silly point, duck, no ball.

NOTE

• Basketball court size: 28 m × 15 m; basket height 10 feet (3.05 m).

• India's basketball body is the Basketball Federation of India (BFI), formed in 1950.

question: India's total length of coastline of the mainland including Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7516.6 km.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The total length of India's coastline, including the mainland, Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep Islands, is 7,516.6 km. (समुद्र तट रेखा)

• The mainland coastline alone measures about 6,100 km.

• Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states (about 1,600 km), followed by Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's total land frontier (land boundary) is about 15,200 km.

• India's total geographical area is 32,87,263 sq km, about 2.4% of the world's land area.

• Nine states and four Union Territories lie along the Indian coast.

NOTE

• India's north–south extent is 3,214 km and east–west extent is 2,933 km.

• The Tropic of Cancer (23°30′N) passes through 8 Indian states; the standard meridian is 82°30′E passing through Mirzapur (UP).

question: The grading system used by the Mughals to fix rank, salary and military responsibilities is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mansabdari system.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar in 1571 (c. 1570s) to fix the rank, salary and military obligations of nobles. (मनसबदारी प्रणाली)

• Each mansabdar held a dual rank — Zat (personal status/salary) and Sawar (number of cavalrymen to be maintained).

• Mansabs ranged from 10 to 10,000; ranks above 5,000 were normally reserved for princes of the royal blood.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Iqta system — land-revenue assignment system of the Delhi Sultanate, introduced by Iltutmish.

• Ryotwari system — British land revenue settlement made directly with the ryot (cultivator), introduced by Thomas Munro/Alexander Read in Madras and Bombay.

• Mahalwari system — revenue settled with the village/mahal as a unit, introduced by Holt Mackenzie (1822) in North-Western Provinces.

NOTE

• Permanent Settlement (1793) — introduced by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha with zamindars as landowners.

• Akbar's revenue system Dahsala/Zabti was implemented by his finance minister Raja Todar Mal.

question: Mallika Sarabhai was awarded with Padma Bhushan (2010) - for contribution to Performing Arts. She was highly recognized for which dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mallika Sarabhai is an eminent Indian dancer and activist trained in Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam. (कुचिपुड़ी और भरतनाट्यम)

• She received the Padma Bhushan in 2010 for her contribution to the performing arts.

• She is the daughter of the classical dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai and space scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, and directs the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts, Ahmedabad.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi — classical dance of Andhra Pradesh; exponents: Raja and Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Vempati Chinna Satyam.

• Bharatanatyam — classical dance of Tamil Nadu; exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy.

• Odissi — Odisha (Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh); Manipuri — Manipur (Jhaveri sisters); Kathakali — Kerala (Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair).

NOTE

• India's eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Sattriya.

• All classical dances derive from Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra.

question: Which of the following dance is particular to the women of the Kamad tribe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Terataal dance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Terataal (Terah Taali) is performed by the women of the Kamad tribe of Rajasthan. (तेरह ताली नृत्य)

• The dancers sit on the floor and strike thirteen manjiras (small brass cymbals) tied to different parts of the body, hence the name *Terah Taali*.

• It is performed in devotion to the folk deity Baba Ramdev (Ramdeoji), usually at Ramdevra.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bhutia dance — associated with the Bhutia community of Sikkim.

• Mask dance (Chham) — a Buddhist monastic dance of Sikkim, Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh.

• Garai/Garia dance — a tribal dance of Tripura performed during the Garia Puja.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan: Ghoomar, Kalbeliya, Kachhi Ghodi, Chari, Bhavai, Gair.

• Kalbeliya dance of Rajasthan was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.

question: What is the currency of Bangladesh, a neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Taka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The currency of Bangladesh is the Taka (BDT). (टका)

• Its capital is Dhaka, and the central bank is the Bangladesh Bank.

• Bangladesh shares the longest land border with India (about 4,096 km), touching West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Yuan (Renminbi) — currency of China; capital Beijing.

• Ngultrum — currency of Bhutan; capital Thimphu.

• Kyat — currency of Myanmar; capital Nay Pyi Taw.

NOTE

• Neighbour currencies: Nepal — Nepalese Rupee; Sri Lanka — Sri Lankan Rupee; Pakistan — Pakistani Rupee; Maldives — Rufiyaa; Afghanistan — Afghani.

• India shares land borders with 7 countries — Bangladesh, China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan.

question: The concept of "Amendment of the Constitution" in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is South Africa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The procedure for amendment of the Constitution and the election of members of the Rajya Sabha were borrowed from the Constitution of South Africa. (संविधान संशोधन की प्रक्रिया)

• Amendment of the Indian Constitution is governed by Article 368 in Part XX.

• The Indian Constitution provides a blend of rigidity and flexibility — amendments by simple majority, special majority, and special majority plus ratification by half the states.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Germany (Weimar) — suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency.

• Canada — federation with a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Centre, appointment of Governors by the Centre.

• Australia — Concurrent List, freedom of trade and commerce, joint sitting of the two Houses.

NOTE

• Britain — parliamentary government, rule of law, single citizenship, writs.

• USA — Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independent judiciary, impeachment of the President, preamble.

• Ireland — DPSP, nomination to Rajya Sabha, method of election of the President; USSR — Fundamental Duties.

question: The Gram Sabha is a meeting of all adults who live in the area covered by a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is panchayat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gram Sabha is the body consisting of all registered voters (adults) in the area of a Gram Panchayat. (ग्राम सभा)

• It is defined in Article 243(b) of the Constitution and is the permanent, foundational unit of the Panchayati Raj system.

• The Gram Sabha approves the panchayat's budget and plans, reviews accounts, and selects beneficiaries of welfare schemes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Panchayati Raj was introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (in force from 24 April 1993), adding Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects).

• Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated at Nagaur, Rajasthan on 2 October 1959 by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, on the recommendation of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957).

• The 74th Amendment Act, 1992 deals with urban local bodies (Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule, 18 subjects).

NOTE

• Panchayati Raj is a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block), Zila Parishad (district).

• Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended a two-tier system; L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) recommended constitutional status for panchayats.

question: As of 2022, who is the India's last living Sadhir dancer honoured with Padma Shri Award in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is R Muthukannammal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• R. Muthukannammal of Viralimalai, Tamil Nadu, is regarded as India's last living Sadhir (Devadasi) dancer and was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for Art. (सादिर नृत्य)

• Sadhir Attam is the older temple-dance tradition of the devadasis from which the modern classical form Bharatanatyam evolved.

• She was initiated into the temple dance tradition as a child and later taught the art to preserve it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Rukmini Devi Arundale — revived and popularised Bharatanatyam and founded Kalakshetra (Chennai, 1936); Padma Bhushan 1956.

• Manjamma Jogati (B. Manjamma Jogati) — transgender folk dancer of the Jogati Nritya of Karnataka; Padma Shri 2021.

• Baisali Mohanty — an Odissi dancer.

NOTE

• Padma Awards order of precedence: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.

• Padma Awards were instituted in 1954 and are announced on Republic Day (26 January).

question: Which freedom fighter of British India is widely regarded as the "father of the two-nation theory"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Syed Ahmed Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (1817–1898) is widely regarded as the father/originator of the Two-Nation Theory, holding that Hindus and Muslims formed two distinct nations. (द्वि-राष्ट्र सिद्धांत)

• He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875, which became Aligarh Muslim University (1920).

• He started the Aligarh Movement for modern, Western education among Muslims and founded the journal Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Muhammad Ali Jinnah — later championed and politically implemented the two-nation theory; passed the Lahore/Pakistan Resolution (1940) and became the first Governor-General of Pakistan.

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak — 'Father of Indian Unrest'; slogan "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"; started Ganapati and Shivaji festivals; papers Kesari and Maratha.

• Jawaharlal Nehru — first Prime Minister of India (1947–1964); author of *Discovery of India*.

NOTE

• The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dhaka by Nawab Salimullah and Aga Khan.

• Separate electorates for Muslims were granted by the Morley–Minto Reforms / Indian Councils Act, 1909.

question: Who presents the annual budget before the Lok Sabha?
option_3: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Union Finance Minister.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Union Budget (Annual Financial Statement) is presented in the Lok Sabha by the Union Finance Minister on behalf of the President. (वार्षिक वित्तीय विवरण)

• The Budget is mentioned in Article 112 of the Constitution as the Annual Financial Statement.

• A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and only on the recommendation of the President (Article 110); the Rajya Sabha can retain it for a maximum of 14 days.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The CAG (Article 148) audits government accounts and is called the guardian of the public purse; he does not present the budget.

• India's first Union Budget was presented by R. K. Shanmukham Chetty on 26 November 1947.

• Morarji Desai presented the highest number of budgets (10).

NOTE

• Since 2017 the budget is presented on 1 February, and the Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget.

• Indira Gandhi was the first woman to present the Union Budget (1970); Nirmala Sitharaman is the first full-time woman Finance Minister to do so (2019).

question: Under which amendment act, article 51A (k) of the Indian constitution was inserted in the constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eighty – sixth amendment Act.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 51A(k) — the duty of a parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the ages of 6 and 14 years — was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002. (मौलिक कर्तव्य)

• It is the 11th Fundamental Duty, the only one added after the original ten.

• The same 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A (Right to Education) as a Fundamental Right and modified Article 45.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• 82nd Amendment Act, 2000 — allowed relaxation in qualifying marks for reservation in promotion for SC/STs.

• 84th Amendment Act, 2001 — froze the readjustment of Lok Sabha/Assembly seats on the basis of the 1991 census till 2026.

• 81st Amendment Act, 2000 — provided for treating backlog vacancies of SC/ST as a separate class (carry forward rule).

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee; originally 10 duties.

• The RTE Act came into force on 1 April 2010.

question: In February 2022, Indian Government launched which operation to bring back Indians stranded in Ukraine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Operation Ganga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Operation Ganga was launched by the Government of India in February 2022 to evacuate Indian citizens, mostly students, stranded in Ukraine after the Russian invasion. (ऑपरेशन गंगा)

• Evacuation flights operated through neighbouring countries — Romania, Hungary, Poland, Slovakia and Moldova.

• Four Union Ministers were sent as Special Envoys to coordinate the evacuation; over 22,500 Indians were brought back.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Operation Flood (1970) — the world's largest dairy development programme, launched by the NDDB under Dr. Verghese Kurien, the 'Father of the White Revolution'.

• Operation Devi Shakti (2021) — evacuation of Indians from Afghanistan.

• Vande Bharat Mission (2020) — repatriation of Indians during the COVID-19 pandemic.

NOTE

• Operation Kaveri (2023) — evacuation of Indians from Sudan.

• Operation Rahat (2015) — evacuation from Yemen; Operation Maitri (2015) — relief in Nepal after the earthquake.

question: Which act was passed by the British Parliament to control the territories of the East India Company majorly in Bengal in the year 1773?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Regulating Act.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first step by the British Parliament to control and regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India. (रेगुलेटिंग एक्ट, 1773)

• It designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal — Lord Warren Hastings was the first — with an Executive Council of four members.

• It provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta (established 1774) with one Chief Justice and three other judges, and made the Bombay and Madras Presidencies subordinate to Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Charter Acts were passed in 1793, 1813, 1833 and 1853; the Charter Act of 1833 made Lord William Bentinck the first Governor-General of India.

• Indian Councils Acts — 1861, 1892, 1909 (Morley–Minto) — dealt with legislative councils and representation.

• Government of India Acts — 1858, 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford), 1935 — transferred power to the Crown and introduced dyarchy/provincial autonomy.

NOTE

• Pitt's India Act, 1784 established a Board of Control and a system of double government.

• The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly except in tea and trade with China.

question: Indian musician Ustad Alla Rakha Qureshi is associated with ___ musical instrument.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Alla Rakha Qureshi (1919–2000) was a legendary tabla maestro of the Punjab gharana. (तबला)

• He is best known for his accompaniment to Pandit Ravi Shankar on the sitar, taking Indian percussion to global audiences.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (1977) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1982); his son Ustad Zakir Hussain is also a world-famous tabla player.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Flute (Bansuri) — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pannalal Ghosh.

• Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, Buddhadev Das Gupta.

• Santoor — Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, Bhajan Sopori.

NOTE

• The tabla is a membranophone (avanaddha vadya); the sitar and sarod are string (tat vadya) instruments; the flute is a wind (sushir vadya) instrument.

• Other instrument-artist pairs: Sitar — Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan; Shehnai — Bismillah Khan; Sarangi — Ram Narayan; Veena — S. Balachander; Mridangam — Palghat Mani Iyer.

question: After the victory over Sakas, who among the following adopted the title of 'Vikramaditya'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chandragupta II (c. 380–415 CE) defeated the Saka (Western Kshatrapa) ruler Rudrasimha III and assumed the title 'Vikramaditya' (also 'Sakari' — destroyer of the Sakas). (विक्रमादित्य)

• His conquest of Gujarat, Kathiawar and Malwa gave the Guptas access to the western sea ports; he made Ujjain a second capital.

• The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during his reign; his court is traditionally associated with the Navaratna, including Kalidasa and Amarasimha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta I — first great Gupta ruler; took the title Maharajadhiraja and married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi.

• Samudragupta — called the 'Napoleon of India' by V.A. Smith; his exploits are recorded in the Allahabad (Prayag) Prashasti by Harisena.

• Skandagupta — repelled the Huna invasion; Kumaragupta I founded Nalanda University and took the title Mahendraditya.

NOTE

• The Gupta period (c. 319–550 CE) is called the Golden Age of India; the Gupta Era was started by Chandragupta I in 319–320 CE.

• The Mehrauli Iron Pillar at Delhi is associated with King Chandra, generally identified with Chandragupta II.

question: "Goitre" is a disease of which of the following glands?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thyroid gland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Goitre is the abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland, caused mainly by a deficiency of iodine in the diet. (घेंघा रोग)

• The thyroid secretes thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), which need iodine; it also secretes calcitonin, which lowers blood calcium.

• Goitre is prevented by using iodised salt; the thyroid is the largest endocrine gland in the human body.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pancreas — a mixed gland; insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus; it also secretes glucagon.

• Adrenal gland — secretes adrenaline (emergency hormone); its deficiency causes Addison's disease.

• Pituitary gland — the 'master gland'; excess growth hormone causes gigantism/acromegaly, deficiency causes dwarfism.

NOTE

• Hypothyroidism in children causes cretinism; in adults it causes myxoedema.

• Hyperthyroidism causes Grave's disease (exophthalmic goitre).

question: The materials, through which things can be seen, are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is transparent materials.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Materials through which things can be seen clearly are called transparent materials. (पारदर्शी पदार्थ)

• They allow almost all light to pass through without scattering — e.g. clear glass, water, air, cellophane.

• Transparency depends on how light is transmitted; transparent objects do not form a dark shadow of their own material.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Opaque materials — do not allow light to pass at all and form sharp shadows, e.g. wood, stone, metal, cardboard.

• Translucent materials — allow partial/diffused light to pass so objects are not clearly seen, e.g. butter paper, frosted glass, oiled paper.

• Conductive materials — allow heat or electricity to pass through, e.g. copper, aluminium; this is unrelated to light transmission.

NOTE

• Light travels in a straight line (rectilinear propagation); a shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light.

• The speed of light in vacuum is 3 × 10⁸ m/s; a luminous body emits its own light (sun), a non-luminous body does not (moon).

question: According to census 2011, what is the population (nearest value) of tribals in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.42 crore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Census 2011, the Scheduled Tribe (tribal) population of India is about 10.43 crore (104 million), i.e. roughly 10.42 crore — about 8.6% of the total population. (अनुसूचित जनजाति)

• The Scheduled Caste population is about 20.14 crore, i.e. 16.6% of the total population.

• Madhya Pradesh has the largest ST population; Mizoram has the highest percentage of STs (about 94.4%); Lakshadweep also has a very high ST share.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India's total population in Census 2011 was 121.08 crore; the decadal growth rate was 17.7%.

• Article 342 empowers the President to specify the Scheduled Tribes of a state or UT.

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th after Independence; its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

NOTE

• Census 2011 — sex ratio 943, literacy 74.04%, density 382 persons/sq km.

• Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest literacy — Kerala; lowest — Bihar.

question: Which of the following is an agro-based industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sugar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Agro-based industries use agricultural produce as raw material; the sugar industry uses sugarcane, so it is agro-based. (कृषि आधारित उद्योग)

• Other agro-based industries: cotton textiles, jute, silk, woollen textiles, vegetable oil, tea, coffee, paper (from bagasse), rubber.

• India is the second largest producer of sugarcane in the world after Brazil; Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are the leading sugar-producing states.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Aluminium and Iron and Steel are mineral-based industries — they use bauxite and iron ore respectively.

• Coal is a mineral/fossil fuel, not an agricultural product; it is the main raw material for thermal power and metallurgical coke.

• India's first modern sugar mill was set up at Betia, Bihar (1903).

NOTE

• Industry classification by raw material: agro-based, mineral-based, marine-based, forest-based.

• Major iron and steel plants: Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), Rourkela (Odisha), Durgapur (WB), Bokaro (Jharkhand), Bhadravati (Karnataka), Jamshedpur/TISCO (Jharkhand).

question: The upper portion of the mantle is called _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is asthenosphere.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The upper portion of the mantle is called the asthenosphere, extending to about 400 km depth. (दुर्बलतामंडल)

• It is the main source of magma that reaches the surface during volcanic eruptions, and its plastic, semi-molten nature allows the movement of tectonic plates.

• The mantle lies between the crust and the core, extending from about 100 km to 2,900 km, and constitutes about 84% of the Earth's volume.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lithosphere — the rigid outer shell comprising the crust and the uppermost solid mantle, about 10–200 km thick; it is broken into tectonic plates.

• Mesosphere — the lower mantle (in geology); in atmospheric science, the layer above the stratosphere where meteors burn up.

• Barysphere — a term used for the interior of the Earth beneath the lithosphere, sometimes for the core.

NOTE

• Earth's core (NiFe/barysphere) extends from 2,900 km to 6,371 km; the outer core is liquid and the inner core solid.

• Discontinuities: Mohorovicic (crust–mantle), Gutenberg (mantle–core), Lehmann (outer–inner core), Conrad (SIAL–SIMA).

question: Olympic Games 1952 were held in which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helsinki.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 1952 Summer Olympics (Games of the XV Olympiad) were held in Helsinki, Finland. (हेलसिंकी, फ़िनलैंड)

• The Soviet Union participated in the Olympics for the first time at these Games.

• India won a bronze medal in wrestling through K. D. Jadhav at Helsinki 1952 — India's first individual Olympic medal; India also won gold in hockey.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• London hosted the Olympics in 1908, 1948 and 2012.

• Berlin hosted the 1936 Olympics, where Jesse Owens won four gold medals.

• New York has never hosted the Olympic Games; the USA hosted them at St. Louis (1904), Los Angeles (1932, 1984) and Atlanta (1996).

NOTE

• The modern Olympics began at Athens in 1896; the IOC was founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin (HQ — Lausanne, Switzerland).

• Olympic motto: "Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter" (Faster, Higher, Stronger – Together).

question: Snails is an example of which of the phylum of animal kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mollusca.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Snails belong to the phylum Mollusca, the second largest phylum of the animal kingdom. (मोलस्का संघ)

• Molluscs have a soft, unsegmented body, usually covered by a calcareous shell, with a muscular foot and a mantle; many possess a rasping organ called the radula.

• Examples: snail, slug, octopus, squid, oyster, mussel, Pila, Chiton.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Arthropoda — the largest phylum; jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton, e.g. cockroach, prawn, spider, butterfly.

• Annelida — metamerically segmented worms with a true coelom, e.g. earthworm, leech, Nereis.

• Protochordates — primitive chordates like Amphioxus (Branchiostoma), Herdmania, Balanoglossus.

NOTE

• Pearls are obtained from the oyster (Pinctada), a mollusc.

• Octopus is the most intelligent mollusc; the giant squid is the largest invertebrate.

question: The famous Pandav Leni Caves is located in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pandav Leni (Pandavleni/Trirashmi) Caves are located near Nashik in Maharashtra. (पांडवलेणी गुफाएँ)

• They form a group of about 24 Buddhist (Hinayana) rock-cut caves carved between the 1st century BCE and the 3rd century CE.

• They contain important inscriptions of the Satavahana, Western Kshatrapa and Abhira rulers, including those of Gautamiputra Satakarni and Nahapana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other famous caves of Maharashtra: Ajanta, Ellora, Elephanta, Karla, Bhaja, Bedse, Kanheri.

• Odisha — Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves (Jain, of King Kharavela).

• Bihar — Barabar Caves, the oldest rock-cut caves, of the Mauryan period, granted to the Ajivikas by Ashoka.

NOTE

• Ajanta (paintings, Buddhist), Ellora (Buddhist, Hindu, Jain — Kailasa temple) and Elephanta (Shaivite, Trimurti) are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

• Nashik on the Godavari river is one of the four venues of the Kumbh Mela.

question: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio was a teacher of which college in 1820s?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindu college, Calcutta.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Henry Louis Vivian Derozio (1809–1831) taught at Hindu College, Calcutta from 1826 to 1831. (हिंदू कॉलेज, कलकत्ता)

• He inspired the radical reformist movement called Young Bengal, and his followers were known as Derozians.

• He promoted free thinking, rationalism and questioning of social orthodoxy, and started the Academic Association; he died of cholera at the age of 22.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Hindu College was founded in 1817 by Raja Rammohan Roy, David Hare and Radhakanta Deb; it later became Presidency College (1855).

• Sanskrit College, Calcutta (1824) is associated with Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, who opened it to non-Brahmin students.

• Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore was founded in 1909 with the support of Jamsetji Tata.

NOTE

• Macaulay's Minute (1835) made English the medium of instruction; Wood's Despatch (1854) is called the Magna Carta of English education in India.

• Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were established in 1857.
